# DOC003 doc-status-header

A document under `docs/` has no status header, a status outside the vocabulary, or a `superseded-by` that names a missing document.

## What it does

Reads the header block of every tracked markdown file under `docs/`: the `Key: value` lines right after the first `# ` title. The `Status:` value must be one of `current`, `draft`, `historical`, `generated` or `superseded-by <document>`, where the document exists beside the page or under `docs/`. Pages that open with the generator marker are exempt, because the generated-file gate already covers them. The finding points at the status line, or at the first line when there is none.

## Why it matters

A reader cannot tell a decided design from a proposal or a retired page unless every page says which it is in the same words, and an index of the documents is only trustworthy when each status is machine readable.

## Remedy

Add `Status: current` (or the right word) under the title, fix the spelling to the vocabulary, or point `superseded-by` at the page that replaced this one.

## Examples

### A document without a status fires

```markdown expect=fire file=docs/design/a.md
# Title <!-- warn: DOC003 -->

No header here.
```

### A status outside the vocabulary fires

```markdown expect=fire file=docs/design/a.md
# Title

Status: DRAFT <!-- warn: DOC003 -->
Owner: frob
```

### A superseded-by naming a missing document fires

```markdown expect=fire file=docs/design/a.md
# Title

Status: superseded-by `gone.md` <!-- warn: DOC003 -->
```

### A status in the vocabulary is clean

```markdown expect=clean file=docs/design/a.md
# Title

Status: current
Owner: frob
```

### A superseded-by naming an existing document is clean

```markdown expect=clean file=docs/design/a.md
# Title

Status: superseded-by `b.md`
```

```markdown file=docs/design/b.md
# Newer

Status: current
```
